key_insight: Post-sampling symbolic constraints turn a plausible diffusion-based trajectory generator into a more admissible one, especially when graph structure becomes complex.
engineering_relevance: For dynamic graph systems in decision support, combining generative models with constraint handling can improve reliability without discarding the benefits of sampling-based uncertainty modeling.
method: Conditional diffusion model generates future graph-state trajectories from partial observations.
External symbolic layer enforces constraints via hard filtering, soft weighting, or projection-based repair.
Evaluation compares structural validity, sample efficiency, diversity, robustness, and calibration on two synthetic graph regimes.
evidence_signal: Invalid probability mass rises from 0.002996 in the compact graph to 0.155929 in the medium-complexity graph; hard filtering removes all invalid retained trajectories while preserving 84.4% of generated samples.
watch_item: Constraint repair or filtering may reduce invalidity, but it can also affect diversity and effective sample size, so deployment should balance admissibility against sampling efficiency.
paper_title: Bridging the Gap Between Plausibility and Admissibility: Constraint-Aware Flow Maps for Dynamic Graph Systems
